cohort: 200 pregnant black South African women, categorized by BMI (overweight/obese vs. non-overweight/non-obese) and HIV status (infected vs. uninfected).
finding: Maternal overweight/obesity was significantly associated with maternal age, gestational age, hypertensive disorders, and anemia, showing increased odds for hypertensive disorders (especially in HIV-infected women) and decreased odds for anemia.
